discovery: Proposal and experimental realization of quantum logic and quantum computing with trapped ions

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / atomic physics / quantum information
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-cooled ions sharing a collective motional mode could perform universal, scalable quantum logic. This was the first concrete physical blueprint for a quantum computer, and it turned quantum information from an abstract idea into a laboratory programme. Rainer Blatt's group then realized it: they implemented the Cirac–Zoller gate, made deterministic teleportation and multi-qubit entangled states with high fidelity, demonstrated quantum error correction, and built programmable digital quantum simulators. Together these advances founded the trapped-ion platform, which still sets the benchmarks for gate fidelity and coherence and is now used in commercial quantum processors. The work also seeded quantum simulation with ions and atoms worldwide. It complements the 2012 prize for controlling individual quantum systems, because it shows how such control becomes coherent multi-particle computation. Its impact is evident in how universally the field has adopted it.
